extraFacts.fact: Column load is the compressive load an extended cylinder and its rod can carry before the rod buckles; it falls as stroke and extended length increase and rises with rod diameter. Push force is working pressure multiplied by the piston (bore) area.
extraFacts.source: Standard mechanics (Euler column buckling; force = pressure x area), as applied in maker hydraulic cylinder catalogues

extraFacts.fact: Pin-to-pin (retracted) length is the distance between the two mounting pin centres with the cylinder fully retracted; extended length is the retracted length plus the stroke.
extraFacts.source: Maker cylinder catalogues; Indus guide to hydraulic cylinder mounting styles

extraFacts.fact: SAE ORB (O-ring boss) ports use a straight thread sealed by an O-ring; NPT ports are tapered pipe threads that seal on the thread.

faqs.a: The Bailey Welded Swivel Eye 1" bore cylinder has a swivel (spherical) eye at the cap end, which tolerates some misalignment between the pins. Fit pins that match the eye or clevis bore, keep the load in line with the cylinder, and make sure the cylinder can swing freely through its full stroke. See our [cylinder mounting styles guide](/blog/hydraulic-cylinder-mounting-styles).

faqs.q: How do I size the Bailey Welded Swivel Eye Hydraulic Cylinder, 1" Bore for my load?
faqs.a: Work out the push force from the working pressure and the 1" bore area, then check the load against the column load for your stroke (the Bailey Welded Swivel Eye 1" bore cylinder lists 2,350 lbs). Retract force is lower because the rod takes up part of the piston area. Our [cylinder force and speed guide](/blog/hydraulic-cylinder-force-and-speed) shows the sums.
